title: Power Apps: form fill assistance using Microsoft 365 files in model-driven apps
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licensing requirements and toolbar automation are supported. Minor corrections should acknowledge the gradual rollout of the environment control, include the environment selection in the maker path, and remove the checklist's unmatched instruction to enable tables.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Microsoft plans to extend form fill assistance in Power Apps model-driven apps to use Microsoft 365 files as a source for form entries.
claims.quote: We’re expanding form fill assistance in Power Apps to use Microsoft 365 files as a source, helping users turn existing content into form entries with less manual effort.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is in development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: The roadmap target is January CY2027.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "January CY2027"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is October CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "October CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Preview as release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.quote: "platforms": ["Android", "iOS", "Web"]

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the arrival default specifically for the Microsoft 365 files extension.
claims.quote: Searched: "form fill" "Microsoft 365 files" "default". Read roadmap, form-filling-assistance, settings-features and Copilot hub; existing upload defaults do not specify the extension's arrival default.

claims.claim: Form fill assistance has a per-user licence entitlement.
claims.quote: The form fill assistance requires specific user licenses based on the product.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: A user of form fill assistance in a Power Apps model-driven app must have a Power Apps premium licence.
claims.quote: Power Apps model-driven app: The user must have a Power Apps premium license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: A user of form fill assistance in a Dynamics 365 model-driven app must have an enterprise or premium licence.
claims.quote: Dynamics 365 model-driven app: The user must have a Dynamics 365 enterprise or premium license as outlined in Dynamics 365 License Guide.

claims.claim: The feature is hidden from users without the required licence.
claims.quote: If the user doesn't have the license, the feature is hidden.

claims.claim: Licence enforcement gradually rolls out following the feature's general availability.
claims.quote: This license enforcement gradually rolls out following the feature's general availability.

claims.claim: Learn describes existing form fill assistance as generally available in Dynamics 365 apps.
claims.quote: This feature is generally available in Dynamics 365 apps.

claims.claim: Learn describes existing form fill assistance as production-ready preview in Power Apps.
claims.quote: This feature is in production ready preview in Power Apps.

claims.claim: Existing form fill assistance can suggest entries based on app usage.
claims.quote: Based on the user's usage of the app, what information is already available in the form, and their frequently used data.

claims.claim: Existing form fill assistance supports smart paste as a source.
claims.quote: Based on the copied text the user provides through the Smart paste capability.

claims.claim: Existing form fill assistance supports files supplied by the user as a source.
claims.quote: Use the file selector button to select the file you want to use to fill in the form. Alternatively, drag and drop the file in the toolbar.

claims.claim: Supported uploaded formats include txt, docx, csv, pdf and images.
claims.quote: Supported file types are .txt, .docx, .csv, .pdf, .png, .jpg, .jpeg, and .bmp.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The existing Files capability does not support sensitivity-labelled files.
claims.quote: Files classified with sensitivity labels aren't supported.

claims.claim: The existing feature's limits have not been confirmed as the design of the Microsoft 365 files extension.
claims.quote: Searched: "form fill assistance" "Microsoft 365 files" licensing default sensitivity locations. Opened form-filling-assistance and its responsible AI FAQ; they describe existing sources, not the planned extension's limits.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented the Microsoft 365 files extension's file-access boundaries.
claims.quote: Searched: "form fill assistance" "Microsoft 365" files source SharePoint OneDrive. Opened form-filling-assistance and its responsible AI FAQ; neither specifies the planned extension's file-access boundaries.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Suggestions are not saved until the user accepts them.
claims.quote: Suggestions are entirely optional and aren't saved in the app until you accept them.

claims.claim: AI suggestions require user review for accuracy before acceptance.
claims.quote: Users are always required to review suggestions and explicitly accept the suggestions that are accurate and appropriate.

claims.claim: Fields with column security are not supported.
claims.quote: Fields that have column security aren't currently supported.

claims.claim: Usage may be throttled.
claims.quote: Usage might be subject to service limits or throttling. Microsoft reserves the right to update the limits.

claims.claim: An additional charge specific to the Microsoft 365 files source is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: "form fill assistance" "Microsoft 365 files" "price"; "Power Apps" "form fill assistance" additional charge credits licensing. Opened form-filling-assistance and Power Platform licensing FAQs; neither publishes an extension-specific charge.

claims.claim: Licensing specific to the Microsoft 365 files source is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Apps" "form fill assistance" "Copilot Credits" licensing guide. Opened form-filling-assistance and Power Platform licensing FAQs; general user licensing is stated, but no separate entitlement for the Microsoft 365 files source is specified.

claims.claim: Learn's existing form fill assistance prerequisites cover web apps with the modern look enabled.
claims.quote: Form fill assistance is available for all apps on the web where the modern, refreshed look is turned on.

claims.claim: The Allow form fill assistance column property must be enabled for a column to receive assistance.
claims.quote: The Allow form fill assistance column property enabled for the column where form fill assistance occurs.

claims.claim: The environment form fill assistance control is at Power Platform admin center > Copilot > Settings > Power Apps > Data entry.
claims.quote: The primary admin control for form fill assistance is moving to the Power Platform admin center under Copilot > Settings > Power Apps > Data entry. Learn more in Copilot hub. This change is gradually rolling out.
claims.fix: Add the row note 'The move to this control is gradually rolling out.' The cited Learn page describes a transition rather than universal availability.

claims.claim: An API for the Copilot Data entry environment control is not documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "Data entry" "Copilot" settings API Power Platform PowerShell pac admin Dataverse; "Copilot" "Data entry" "Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironment". Read Copilot hub, pac env, organization reference and Environment Management Settings tutorial; no matching control property.

claims.claim: The app toolbar control is reached through Solutions > solution > Apps > app > Edit > Settings > Features > Form fill assist toolbar.
claims.quote: When you select Settings from the command bar, select Features to enable or disable model-driven app features for the app. ... Form fill assist toolbar.
claims.fix: Use 'environment > Solutions > solution > Apps > app > Edit > Settings > Features > Form fill assist toolbar'. The cited create-edit-app page's 'Edit an app' section confirms the existing entry steps and first says to choose the environment.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: Xrm.Utility.getGlobalContext().saveSettingValue("FormFileUploadEnabled", true, { overrideScope: 2, solutionUniqueName: "<solution>" }) sets the app-level toolbar setting.
claims.quote: Xrm.Utility.getGlobalContext().saveSettingValue(settingName, value, saveSettingOptions).then(successCallback, errorCallback); ... Use 2 to add or update a setting app value.

claims.claim: App setting changes in the designer should be saved and published.
claims.quote: You must select Publish to activate an app settings change. ... Save and Publish the app.

claims.claim: Neither an admin UI nor automation is documented for a switch specific to Microsoft 365 files as a source.
claims.quote: Searched: "form fill assistance" "Microsoft 365 files" "settings". Read form-filling-assistance, settings-features, app-properties, client setting API, Copilot hub and organization reference; no switch specific to this source is documented.

claims.claim: Makers can configure Allow form fill assistance (preview) per column.
claims.quote: Allow form fill assistance (preview) | This is a preview feature. When enabled, users receive suggestions generated by AI for columns that support form fill assistance in main and quick create forms.

claims.claim: The column property can be disabled for columns that might contain sensitive information.
claims.quote: You can disable for columns that might contain sensitive information, such as email address.

claims.claim: The Power Platform admin center's Copilot hub shows usage for the data entry agent.
claims.quote: Admins can view usage analytics for the data entry agent and data exploration agent on the Power Apps page to understand the value that end users are getting from AI in Power Apps.

claims.claim: The supported Microsoft 365 file locations for the extension remain unspecified.
claims.quote: Searched: "form fill assistance" "Microsoft 365" files source SharePoint OneDrive. Opened form-filling-assistance and FAQ about form fill assistance; neither names Microsoft 365 file locations for the roadmap extension.

claims.claim: Whether the Microsoft 365 files extension honours sensitivity labels remains undocumented.
claims.quote: Searched: "form fill assistance" "Microsoft 365 files" licensing default sensitivity locations. Opened form-filling-assistance and its FAQ; the existing Files capability excludes labelled files, but neither documents label handling for the extension.

claims.claim: The checklist's instruction to enable tables has a corresponding control in the controls table.
claims.quote: Enable for a pilot app and tables first. | Controls: Form fill assistance (data entry agent) per environment; Form fill assist toolbar for an app; Switch specific to Microsoft 365 files as a source.
claims.fix: Replace 'Enable for a pilot app and tables first.' with 'Enable for a pilot app first.' The table has no table-level control; do not add a row.
